mentions.name: Stone Tools
mentions.description: A blog exploring retro productivity software from the 1977–1995 era, with the author spending at least two weeks hands-on with each title to learn it, build things with it, and understand its approach to solving problems. Unlike most retrocomputing writing, it deliberately skips games and isn't tied to any single machine, and each article adds tangents into related computing history in a casual, conversational tone.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm continuing to build a body of work on my retro productivity software blog, Stone Tools.

mentions.name: Stone Tools
mentions.description: A blog exploring the productivity software of the 8/16-bit computing era, offering light-hearted but heartfelt assessments of classic programs' form and function both for their time and today. Posts are based on hands-on use of the software and also explore related threads, such as the legacy and promise of the paperless office; published monthly with the goal of building a regular readership.
mentions.problem: Retrocomputing discourse is heavily centered on gaming, leaving the productivity software of the 8/16-bit era underexplored.
